claims: Copilot CLI supports Agent Plugins 1.0 and legacy Copilot manifests.
Legacy manifests may explicitly configure skills and agents paths.
Local plugin installs are cached; reinstall to pick up edits.
Use plugin list, /skills list and /agent to verify discovery.
limitations: This port chooses documented legacy component paths, not Agent Plugins namespaced paths.
CLI discovery was not executed in the sandbox.

claims: CLI accepts exact Agent Plugins 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 schema URLs, with fixed skills/ and com.github.copilot/agents/ paths.
Legacy agents use .agent.md files and may configure component paths.
Direct installation supports OWNER/REPO:PATH and absolute local paths.
Marketplace manifests are supported, but not required for direct installs.
Portable MCP components and Copilot-specific namespaces have separate semantics.
limitations: Original Cursor .cursor-plugin metadata is not a Copilot manifest.
The archived root Agent Plugins manifest is a supported format in principle, but cannot load root agents/ with Copilot Agent Plugins semantics.

claims: Skills support name, description, user-invocable, disable-model-invocation, argument-hint and allowed-tools.
disable-model-invocation prevents automatic invocation; user-invocable independently controls manual slash invocation.
CLI duplicate skills can use plugin-qualified slash invocation names; inspect the actual list.
CLI has a task tool and list_agents/read_agent/write_agent; these are not the Cursor Task call contract.
CLI custom agents support model, models, modelPolicy and reasoningEffort.
CLI background task controls include /tasks and Ctrl+X then b; sidekick agents are a separate native feature.
Custom CLI subagents do not inherit repository instructions by default; include-custom-instructions opts in.
Model selection, permissions, sandboxing and available tools remain host-controlled.
limitations: No portable mapping was verified for Cursor subagent_type, readonly, run_in_background, is_background, AskQuestion, todo tools, /loop or /in-cloud.
This port defaults to sequential role passes and inherited models; no hardcoded Cursor model IDs or fabricated APIs.

claims: ~/.copilot/settings.json is the CLI user settings file; config.json is internal state.
CLI user subagents.agents.<id>.model and effortLevel have actual documented consumers.
.github/copilot/settings.json and settings.local.json accept only a supported repository subset; unknown keys are ignored.
Repository enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces support declarative plugin adoption.
limitations: An arbitrary renamed pstack-models file has no automatic loader.
User settings, repository settings and custom-agent frontmatter are not interchangeable.
Company policy may override local preferences.

claims: Repository skills live in .github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md.
Skills bundle instructions, scripts and resources and load when relevant.
limitations: Common skill discovery does not establish tool, MCP, model or background execution parity.

claims: Skill names use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens and match the directory.
user-invocable and disable-model-invocation independently control manual and automatic availability.
VS Code prefixes plugin skill slash commands with a plugin namespace.
limitations: Background knowledge is not background process execution.
Do not promise identical slash command spelling across CLI and VS Code.

claims: VS Code documents Agent Plugins 1.0, source installs, marketplaces and local plugin locations.
CLI-installed plugins can be discovered by VS Code.
limitations: VS Code customization interfaces and CLI /plugin commands maintain separate inventories.
This legacy CLI package is not claimed integration-tested in VS Code; use managed project skills for the documented common path.

claims: Portable tool aliases include read, search, edit, execute and agent.
A tools list controls availability, not approval.
Cloud ignores custom-agent handoffs and argument-hint.
limitations: An omitted tools list exposes all session-available tools; not a read-only security boundary.
CLI model/effort extensions are not assumed portable.

claims: Copilot supports native hook events and structured permission decisions.
CLI preToolUse command failures fail closed, but hook timeouts fail open.
Cloud is noninteractive; permissionRequest is not an effective cloud approval gate.
limitations: This port does not bundle hooks or translate Cursor automation triggers.
Prompt comments and optional hooks are not security boundaries.

claims: CLI MCP servers require explicit configuration and appropriate trust/authentication.
Trusted project MCP configuration is distinct from VS Code's configuration envelope.
limitations: No upstream private/internal MCP availability is implied or provisioned.
Missing tools must stop the affected workflow rather than fabricate results.

claims: Cloud supports configured MCP tools with network and secret constraints.
MCP resources/prompts and OAuth-authenticated remote servers are not currently supported.
limitations: Private Cursor infrastructure and credentials are not fetched.
Cloud runtime and plugin installation were not exercised in this sandbox.

claims: GitHub documents plugins across Copilot clients, including declarative cloud adoption through repository plugin settings.
Portable components do not imply portable harness behavior.
limitations: No claim of feature parity or automatic cloud adoption is made by this port.
